Playbook.name: Linux — Credential File Modified (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group) - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A Linux credential/authorisation file (/etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group or /etc/sudoers) was created, updated or moved, observed by File Integrity Monitoring (logs-fim.event-*, verified live: these paths are watched on ~49 hosts). The triage question is whether this is legitimate account/package administration or an attacker adding a backdoor account, changing a password hash, granting a group/sudo right, or reading shadow for offline cracking. IMPORTANT JCB CONSTRAINT (verified live): FIM records the file change but NOT the actor — user.name and process.name are 0% populated on these events. Attribution of WHO changed the file requires correlating auditd USER_CMD records on the same host, which capture only sudo-invoked commands.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Direct modification of these files creates persistent backdoor accounts, resets privileged passwords, or silently grants sudo/group rights on core-banking Linux hosts. Reading /etc/shadow enables offline password cracking of every local account. Any of these undermines the trust boundary of the host.

Assets.AssetType: Linux servers (core banking, application, database — INTDOM)

LogSources.LogSource: Elastic File Integrity Monitoring — logs-fim.event-* (verified live: /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group, /etc/sudoers watched; event.action, file.path, file.hash.sha1, file.size, file.owner populated)
Linux auditd USER_CMD records — logs-auditd.log-* (verified live: sudo commands with process.args and auditd.log.AUID — used for actor attribution)

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FIM shipping to logs-fim.event-* with the credential files under watch (verified live).
ACTOR NOT IN FIM: user.name and process.name are null on FIM file events (verified live) — FIM answers WHAT/WHEN, not WHO. Use auditd USER_CMD for the actor.

PARTIAL ACTOR COVERAGE: JCB Linux auditd does NOT audit execve or file syscalls (verified: auditd_manager emits no exec/executed actions). auditd USER_CMD captures only sudo-invoked commands — a change made while already root, or by a non-sudo daemon, has no actor record. Full attribution needs auditd execve+file auditing or Elastic Defend / MDE-for-Linux device telemetry.

Signal.Name: Credential file changed
Signal.Details: event.action created/updated/moved on /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group or /etc/sudoers in logs-fim.event-*. file.path is the affected file; file.hash.sha1 / file.size / file.owner characterise the change.

Signal.Name: Attributable sudo edit
Signal.Details: A matching auditd USER_CMD on the same host (vipw/vigr/usermod/chpasswd/passwd/editor against the file) names the invoking user via auditd.log.AUID.

Input.name: $hostname
Input.description: Linux host where the credential file changed (host.name from the alert).

ImmediateCapture.Item: Which file changed (file.path) and the action (created/updated/moved) from the alert
Change window (first_seen/last_seen) to align the auditd USER_CMD correlation

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance — a single FIM event alone cannot tell you intent because the actor is not in the FIM record.

If /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow and /etc/group all changed together alongside many other /etc or /usr files (INV-03), lean toward package/user-management tooling. A lone /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers change is more targeted.

Investigation.Goal: Decide whether the credential-file modification on $hostname is legitimate account/package administration or attacker account-manipulation / credential access, using FIM for the WHAT and auditd USER_CMD for the WHO.

Step.name: Reconstruct the credential-file change (FIM)
Step.Purpose: Confirm exactly which credential files changed on $hostname, how, when, and how the file looks now — the anchor facts. FIM is the authoritative WHAT/WHEN source.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND file.path IN ("/etc/passwd","/etc/shadow","/etc/group","/etc/sudoers") AND event.action IN ("created","updated","moved") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp), actions = VALUES(event.action), sha1s = VALUES(file.hash.sha1), sizes = VALUES(file.size), owners = VALUES(file.owner) BY file.path | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A change to /etc/shadow (password hashes) or /etc/sudoers (privilege) is higher-risk than /etc/group. Multiple sha1 values in the window = the file was rewritten more than once. Record first_seen/last_seen — you will align the auditd USER_CMD search (INV-02) to this window.

Step.name: Attribute the actor via sudo (auditd USER_CMD)
Step.Purpose: FIM has no actor. auditd USER_CMD is the only JCB telemetry that names WHO ran a command touching these files — but only when it was run via sudo.
Step.Query: FROM logs-auditd.log-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND auditd.log.record_type == "USER_CMD" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cmd = MV_CONCAT(process.args, " ") | WHERE cmd RLIKE ".*(/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|/etc/group|/etc/sudoers|passwd|usermod|chpasswd|vipw|vigr|visudo).*" | KEEP @timestamp, auditd.log.AUID, auditd.log.UID, process.executable, cmd, host.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: A sudo edit by an unexpected AUID with no IAM justification is account manipulation. A known admin running useradd/passwd/usermod as documented maintenance is benign. NO rows here does NOT clear the alert — the change may have been made while already root or by a non-sudo process, which auditd does not capture; escalate to on-host inspection in that case.

Step.name: Was the change isolated or part of a bulk system update
Step.Purpose: Separate a targeted credential edit from a package/user-management sweep. A yum/dnf update or bulk provisioning rewrites passwd/shadow/group alongside many other files; a lone credential-file change does not.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fim.event-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND event.action IN ("created","updated","moved") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY file.path | SORT changes DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: Many concurrent /etc and /usr/lib changes around the same timestamps indicate a package transaction or configuration-management run (benign). Only the credential files changing, with nothing else, is a targeted-modification signal that raises suspicion.

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows a sudo edit of /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers (or usermod/chpasswd on passwd) by an AUID that is not an authorised administrator, with no IAM/change justification.
Node.Result: True Positive (Account Manipulation / backdoor or privilege grant — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows /etc/shadow was read/rewritten and INV-03 shows the change is isolated (no package sweep), and the actor cannot be tied to authorised maintenance.
Node.Result: True Positive (Credential Access — shadow tampering/harvest — escalate to IR)

Node.Condition: INV-02 names a known admin AUID running documented user-management (useradd/passwd) OR INV-03 shows the credential files changed as part of a bulk package/config-management transaction under a change record.
A provisioning/configuration-management tool (e.g. Ansible/Puppet service account) edited the accounts per a known job whose scope matches INV-03.
Node.Result: Misconfiguration (Automation over-managing accounts — fix the job, do not blanket-exception)

Node.Condition: FIM confirms the change but INV-02 returns no actor (change made as root or via a non-sudo process, outside auditd coverage) and intent cannot be established remotely.
Node.Result: Needs Escalation (inspect the host directly — coverage gap)

FalsePositive.Definition: A legitimate administrator or approved automation changed the credential file as part of documented account or package administration — never simply "the file changed"; the authorising context must be shown.

Indicators.Item: INV-02 names a known admin AUID with a matching maintenance/change ticket.
INV-03 shows the credential files changed alongside a package transaction (many concurrent /etc, /usr changes).
Resulting file state (owner/size) is consistent with a normal account addition.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the admin identity and the ticket; close as false_positive.
If a recurring provisioning account trips the rule, propose a scoped exception for that AUID/host only — not a rule disable.

TruePositive.Definition: An adversary modified a credential/authorisation file to persist (backdoor account, added sudo/group right), change a privileged password, or harvest /etc/shadow for offline cracking.

Indicators.Item: Sudo edit by an unexpected/unauthorised AUID (INV-02), or no legitimate actor and an isolated change (INV-03).
/etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers targeted specifically, outside any change window.
On-host inspection reveals a new/unknown account entry, NOPASSWD sudo grant, or altered hash.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; inspect the file on-disk for the exact added/changed entry; preserve the file and auditd/FIM evidence.
Treat the invoking AUID (and any account added) as compromised; reset credentials; hunt the same pattern on peer hosts.

Misconfiguration.Definition: Internal automation edited accounts via sudo more broadly or at the wrong time — operationally driven, not malicious.

Indicators.Item: A service/automation AUID performed the edit on a schedule.
Change breadth matches a known provisioning job that caught files it should not have.

SOCAction.Item: Engage the automation owner to correct scope/timing; revert any wrongly-added entries.
Track under identity hygiene; do not blanket-exception the rule.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: From INV-01 confirm which files changed and the window; from INV-02 identify the actor if a sudo record exists.
If the actor is unauthorised or unattributable and the change is isolated, isolate $hostname and inspect the file on-disk before anything is overwritten.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Capture the current /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow, /etc/group, /etc/sudoers and the surrounding session on-host; identify and remove any backdoor account or unauthorised sudo/group grant.
Reset credentials for the invoking user and any account added/changed; sweep peer Linux hosts for the same modification.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable auditd execve+file (watch) auditing on /etc credential files, OR ingest Elastic Defend / MDE-for-Linux device telemetry, so future changes carry the actor natively rather than needing USER_CMD correlation.
Review who holds sudo rights to edit these files; restrict and monitor as a higher-severity correlated analytic.

Escalation.Trigger: Unauthorised or unattributable sudo edit of /etc/shadow or /etc/sudoers, an isolated targeted change with no package context, or on-host discovery of a backdoor account / NOPASSWD grant.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Actor and change confirmed as authorised administration or a package/provisioning transaction, with a matching ticket.
Resulting file state reviewed and consistent with the documented change.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host isolated and inspected; backdoor account / unauthorised grant / altered hash removed; evidence preserved.
Involved credentials reset; peer hosts swept; incident documented and coverage gap (root/non-sudo edits) recorded.
